observations: Texas Instruments reported first-half 2026 revenue of $10.29B, up 21% year over year, driven primarily by Analog and secondarily Embedded Processing demand.
Q2 2026 Analog revenue was $4.365B, up 26% year over year, with operating margin 45.6%; Embedded Processing revenue was $788M, up 16%, with operating margin 21.3%.
First-half operating cash flow was $4.22B, up $1.51B year over year; capital expenditures were $1.19B versus $2.43B in the prior-year period.

The filing states higher manufacturing costs associated with planned capacity expansions partially offset gross-profit growth; 2026 CHIPS Act incentives provided $1.10B of cash proceeds in the first half.
Inventory was $4.61B at June 30, 2026, down $199M from year-end 2025; days of inventory declined to 196 from 222.

risks.risk: Capacity expansion remains a fixed-cost and return-on-capital risk if broad analog/embedded demand recovery weakens; the filing explicitly notes higher manufacturing costs from planned capacity expansions.

unknowns.unknown: The filing does not by itself establish current peer-relative valuation or quantify incremental returns/utilization for each new 300mm fab; Alpha must underwrite those separately.
